API Access

Programmatic access to DevFathom for integrations, automation, and AI assistants like Claude Code.

1 · Get an API token

API tokens are issued by an admin from Settings → API Tokens. Each token is bound to a specific user — every change made with it is logged to the activity feed and counted in stats under that user.

Ask an admin to create a token for you, pick the scopes you need (e.g. tasks:read + tasks:write), and they'll share the token with you. The full token is shown only once.

2 · Fetch the full API reference

The full machine-readable spec — every endpoint, every field, every scope, plus common workflow recipes — lives at a single URL and requires your token to access:

curl https://sehatcart.pharmacy.develop.devfathom.com/api/v1/spec \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer df_your_token_here"

Returns a Markdown document optimized for LLM agents. Hand the URL + your token to Claude Code (or Cursor, or any agent) and it has everything it needs to operate the hub.

3 · Use with Claude Code

Drop this in a CLAUDE.md at the root of any project where you want to use the hub:

# DevFathom API

Token: ${DEVFATHOM_TOKEN}
Reference: https://sehatcart.pharmacy.develop.devfathom.com/api/v1/spec

To use the hub, fetch the reference above with the token, then make
authenticated requests against https://sehatcart.pharmacy.develop.devfathom.com/api/v1/* per the spec.

All changes I make are logged as the user this token is bound to.

Then export the token and start a session:

export DEVFATHOM_TOKEN="df_..."
claude
Attribution: The token acts as the user it was bound to. If Shehroz's token creates a task, the activity feed shows “Shehroz created task X” and it counts toward Shehroz's stats.
Security

Treat tokens like passwords. Never commit them. Store them in env vars or a secrets manager.

If you suspect a token is exposed, ask an admin to revoke it from Settings → API Tokens. Revocation is immediate.

Definition and limits

First observed qualifying original completed receipt across all available data in selected authorized branches; not first-ever customers. Enrollment dates are inclusive UTC days, clipped at the frozen as-of instant. Follow-up uses elapsed 24-hour days; a repeat is a distinct receipt strictly later than first observation, at or before the horizon boundary.

Qualification requires a receipt number, completion timestamp, positive original line value and remaining original units after posted returns, with posted refunds below original line value, all as of cutoff. Partial reversals can qualify. Returns and refunds have no direct matching link: these are independent exclusion tests, not a reconciled net-revenue measure. Current sale status and commercial identity are used; past status/identity changes cannot be reconstructed. Data start, missing receipts, ingestion delays, outages and off-system purchases are unknown; elapsed follow-up does not prove complete observation. No adherence, competitor churn or uplift inference. Anonymous receipts remain in coverage totals, outside person rates. All available selected history is aggregated in the database; receipt and detail counts are not truncated. Reports exceeding the 10-second database execution budget fail without partial rates. Large branch or chain histories may still exceed this budget; narrower enrollment dates do not reduce the history required.

API Access

Programmatic access to DevFathom for integrations, automation, and AI assistants like Claude Code.

1 · Get an API token

API tokens are issued by an admin from Settings → API Tokens. Each token is bound to a specific user — every change made with it is logged to the activity feed and counted in stats under that user.

Ask an admin to create a token for you, pick the scopes you need (e.g. tasks:read + tasks:write), and they'll share the token with you. The full token is shown only once.

2 · Fetch the full API reference

The full machine-readable spec — every endpoint, every field, every scope, plus common workflow recipes — lives at a single URL and requires your token to access:

curl https://sehatcart.pharmacy.develop.devfathom.com/api/v1/spec \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer df_your_token_here"

Returns a Markdown document optimized for LLM agents. Hand the URL + your token to Claude Code (or Cursor, or any agent) and it has everything it needs to operate the hub.

3 · Use with Claude Code

Drop this in a CLAUDE.md at the root of any project where you want to use the hub:

# DevFathom API

Token: ${DEVFATHOM_TOKEN}
Reference: https://sehatcart.pharmacy.develop.devfathom.com/api/v1/spec

To use the hub, fetch the reference above with the token, then make
authenticated requests against https://sehatcart.pharmacy.develop.devfathom.com/api/v1/* per the spec.

All changes I make are logged as the user this token is bound to.

Then export the token and start a session:

export DEVFATHOM_TOKEN="df_..."
claude
Attribution: The token acts as the user it was bound to. If Shehroz's token creates a task, the activity feed shows “Shehroz created task X” and it counts toward Shehroz's stats.
Security

Treat tokens like passwords. Never commit them. Store them in env vars or a secrets manager.

If you suspect a token is exposed, ask an admin to revoke it from Settings → API Tokens. Revocation is immediate.

Definition and limits

First observed qualifying original completed receipt across all available data in selected authorized branches; not first-ever customers. Enrollment dates are inclusive UTC days, clipped at the frozen as-of instant. Follow-up uses elapsed 24-hour days; a repeat is a distinct receipt strictly later than first observation, at or before the horizon boundary.

Qualification requires a receipt number, completion timestamp, positive original line value and remaining original units after posted returns, with posted refunds below original line value, all as of cutoff. Partial reversals can qualify. Returns and refunds have no direct matching link: these are independent exclusion tests, not a reconciled net-revenue measure. Current sale status and commercial identity are used; past status/identity changes cannot be reconstructed. Data start, missing receipts, ingestion delays, outages and off-system purchases are unknown; elapsed follow-up does not prove complete observation. No adherence, competitor churn or uplift inference. Anonymous receipts remain in coverage totals, outside person rates. All available selected history is aggregated in the database; receipt and detail counts are not truncated. Reports exceeding the 10-second database execution budget fail without partial rates. Large branch or chain histories may still exceed this budget; narrower enrollment dates do not reduce the history required.

API Access

Programmatic access to DevFathom for integrations, automation, and AI assistants like Claude Code.

1 · Get an API token

API tokens are issued by an admin from Settings → API Tokens. Each token is bound to a specific user — every change made with it is logged to the activity feed and counted in stats under that user.

Ask an admin to create a token for you, pick the scopes you need (e.g. tasks:read + tasks:write), and they'll share the token with you. The full token is shown only once.

2 · Fetch the full API reference

The full machine-readable spec — every endpoint, every field, every scope, plus common workflow recipes — lives at a single URL and requires your token to access:

curl https://sehatcart.pharmacy.develop.devfathom.com/api/v1/spec \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer df_your_token_here"

Returns a Markdown document optimized for LLM agents. Hand the URL + your token to Claude Code (or Cursor, or any agent) and it has everything it needs to operate the hub.

3 · Use with Claude Code

Drop this in a CLAUDE.md at the root of any project where you want to use the hub:

# DevFathom API

Token: ${DEVFATHOM_TOKEN}
Reference: https://sehatcart.pharmacy.develop.devfathom.com/api/v1/spec

To use the hub, fetch the reference above with the token, then make
authenticated requests against https://sehatcart.pharmacy.develop.devfathom.com/api/v1/* per the spec.

All changes I make are logged as the user this token is bound to.

Then export the token and start a session:

export DEVFATHOM_TOKEN="df_..."
claude
Attribution: The token acts as the user it was bound to. If Shehroz's token creates a task, the activity feed shows “Shehroz created task X” and it counts toward Shehroz's stats.
Security

Treat tokens like passwords. Never commit them. Store them in env vars or a secrets manager.

If you suspect a token is exposed, ask an admin to revoke it from Settings → API Tokens. Revocation is immediate.

Definition and limits

First observed qualifying original completed receipt across all available data in selected authorized branches; not first-ever customers. Enrollment dates are inclusive UTC days, clipped at the frozen as-of instant. Follow-up uses elapsed 24-hour days; a repeat is a distinct receipt strictly later than first observation, at or before the horizon boundary.

Qualification requires a receipt number, completion timestamp, positive original line value and remaining original units after posted returns, with posted refunds below original line value, all as of cutoff. Partial reversals can qualify. Returns and refunds have no direct matching link: these are independent exclusion tests, not a reconciled net-revenue measure. Current sale status and commercial identity are used; past status/identity changes cannot be reconstructed. Data start, missing receipts, ingestion delays, outages and off-system purchases are unknown; elapsed follow-up does not prove complete observation. No adherence, competitor churn or uplift inference. Anonymous receipts remain in coverage totals, outside person rates. All available selected history is aggregated in the database; receipt and detail counts are not truncated. Reports exceeding the 10-second database execution budget fail without partial rates. Large branch or chain histories may still exceed this budget; narrower enrollment dates do not reduce the history required.

API Access

Programmatic access to DevFathom for integrations, automation, and AI assistants like Claude Code.

1 · Get an API token

API tokens are issued by an admin from Settings → API Tokens. Each token is bound to a specific user — every change made with it is logged to the activity feed and counted in stats under that user.

Ask an admin to create a token for you, pick the scopes you need (e.g. tasks:read + tasks:write), and they'll share the token with you. The full token is shown only once.

2 · Fetch the full API reference

The full machine-readable spec — every endpoint, every field, every scope, plus common workflow recipes — lives at a single URL and requires your token to access:

curl https://sehatcart.pharmacy.develop.devfathom.com/api/v1/spec \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer df_your_token_here"

Returns a Markdown document optimized for LLM agents. Hand the URL + your token to Claude Code (or Cursor, or any agent) and it has everything it needs to operate the hub.

3 · Use with Claude Code

Drop this in a CLAUDE.md at the root of any project where you want to use the hub:

# DevFathom API

Token: ${DEVFATHOM_TOKEN}
Reference: https://sehatcart.pharmacy.develop.devfathom.com/api/v1/spec

To use the hub, fetch the reference above with the token, then make
authenticated requests against https://sehatcart.pharmacy.develop.devfathom.com/api/v1/* per the spec.

All changes I make are logged as the user this token is bound to.

Then export the token and start a session:

export DEVFATHOM_TOKEN="df_..."
claude
Attribution: The token acts as the user it was bound to. If Shehroz's token creates a task, the activity feed shows “Shehroz created task X” and it counts toward Shehroz's stats.
Security

Treat tokens like passwords. Never commit them. Store them in env vars or a secrets manager.

If you suspect a token is exposed, ask an admin to revoke it from Settings → API Tokens. Revocation is immediate.
